**Finding: deviation (high severity) — §2 Grant of License (p0028)**

- **Not revocable at will:** §17(a) makes the licence perpetual while fees are paid, and termination is limited to insolvency events or material breach with a 30-day cure (p0127); §17 even converts the licence to a fee-free perpetual licence if we terminate for Garman's default. That part meets the playbook.
- **Affiliates:** covered only where "operating at Authorized Locations" — narrower than our position.
- **Contractors:** not covered at all, and §3(c)/(e) bar sublicensing or use beyond what is authorised.
- **Transferability:** grant is expressly "non-transferable", reinforced by §3(c) and §20(d) consent requirement — no successor path.

Redline validated (ok:true) and submitted: the grant now runs to Sparkling, its affiliated companies and contractors acting on its behalf (with Sparkling responsible for their compliance), drops "non-transferable", and permits transfer to a successor of all or substantially all of the business, with the fallback (affiliates on written notice) flagged in the comment.

Rule:
ID: LICENSE
Title: Licence grant scope
Kind: parametric
Summary: The licence must cover our affiliates and contractors and must not be revocable at will.
Severity: high
Category: licence
Position — preferred:
Licence extends to Customer's affiliates and to contractors acting on Customer's behalf; paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable; subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach; transferable to successors.

Position — fallback:
Affiliates covered on written notice; transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
Position — walk-away:
Licence revocable at Vendor's discretion; affiliates and contractors excluded with no path to add them.
Detection guidance:
Find the grant clause: "non-exclusive, non-transferable", "revocable", "solely for Customer's internal use", whether affiliates/contractors are named, term of the licence.

Redline guidance:
Insert "and its Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf", delete "revocable", add successor transfer.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
The licence is perpetual while fees are paid and terminable only on insolvency or uncured material breach (§17), so it is not revocable at will. However, the grant covers affiliates only where they operate at Authorized Locations, omits contractors acting on our behalf, and is expressly "non-transferable" with assignment barred absent Garman's consent (§3(c), §20(d)), leaving no successor path. The redline extends the grant to affiliates and contractors (with us responsible for their compliance) and permits transfer to a successor of the business, matching the preferred position.

Original paragraphs:
p0028: Garman hereby grants to Sparkling, for the use of Sparkling and affiliated companies of Sparkling operating at Authorized Locations, a non-transferable and non-exclusive licence to use: (i) the Software, safely in executable object code format, at each AS400 at each of the Authorized Locations; and (ii) the Documentation. Sparkling's right, if any, to use the Software and Documentation at locations other than the Authorized Locations is subject to the payment of additional fees in accordance with the Fee Schedule.
p0033: (c) not assign this Agreement or transfer, lease, export or grant a sublicence of the Work to any Person, except as and when authorized to do so by Garman in writing;
p0142: (d) Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights and obligations under this Agreement to any third party without the written consent of the other party.

Resolved definitions:
none

Rendered redline:
p0028: Garman hereby grants to Sparkling, for the use of Sparkling, its affiliated companies and contractors acting on Sparkling's behalf (Sparkling remaining responsible for their compliance with this Agreement), a non-exclusive licence, transferable to a successor to all or substantially all of Sparkling's business by merger, acquisition or sale of assets, to use: (i) the Software, safely in executable object code format, at each AS400 at each of the Authorized Locations; and (ii) the Documentation. content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation on § 13 (¶ p0088).**

What I found:
- **Vendor claims our paid-for deliverables.** § 13 gives Garman ownership of all IP in the Work "including any Improvements or **Modifications** thereto". "Modifications" is defined (§ 1(f)) as the changes set out in Schedule "D" — bespoke work we commission and pay for. That breaches the preferred position that we own what we pay for.
- **No licence back.** The § 2 grant covers only the "Software" and "Documentation" (Schedule "B"), so the Schedule "D" Modifications arguably fall outside the licence entirely — vendor ownership with no clear right of use for us.
- **Customer Data is unaddressed.** Garman converts, processes and stores our data under § 4(b), but nothing in the agreement confirms we retain all rights in it; § 14 confidentiality is not an ownership provision, and the § 16 escrow only supports continuity.
- Garman's ownership of its own routing platform is acceptable under the rule, so I left that intact.

Redline (validated ok:true) makes a single-paragraph edit that removes "Modifications" from Garman's ownership claim, assigns customer-funded Modifications and deliverables to Sparkling with a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence back for any embedded Garman pre-existing IP, confirms our data and materials remain ours, and bars joint ownership. The comment offers the fallback (Garman ownership plus a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense).

Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Section 13 gives Garman ownership of all IP in the Work "including any Improvements or Modifications thereto". "Modifications" are the bespoke changes set out in Schedule "D" that we commission and pay for (Sections 1(f), 4 and the Fee Schedule), so as drafted Garman owns the deliverables created for us, and because the Section 2 licence covers only the "Software" and "Documentation" (Schedules "B") there is not even a clear licence back to the Modifications. The agreement is also silent on ownership of our data, which Garman converts and processes under Section 4(b) — nothing confirms we retain all rights in it. Garman retaining ownership of its own routing platform is acceptable, so the redline leaves that intact and only (i) assigns customer-funded Modifications and deliverables to us with a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence back for any embedded Garman pre-existing IP, (ii) confirms our data and materials remain ours, and (iii) excludes joint ownership. Fallback offered in the comment is Garman ownership plus a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense the Modifications.

Original paragraphs:
p0088: Garman is the owner of all intellectual property rights in the Work (including any Improvements or Modifications thereto), including all related materials, logos, and names provided pursuant to the terms of this Agreement. No title to the intellectual property in the Work is transferred to Sparkling by this Agreement.

Resolved definitions:
none

Rendered redline:
p0088: Garman is the owner of all intellectual property rights in the Work (including any Improvements thereto), including all related materials, logos, and names provided pursuant to the terms of this Agreement. Except as expressly set out in this Section 13, no title to the intellectual property in the Work is transferred to Sparkling by this Agreement. Garman hereby assigns to Sparkling all intellectual property rights in the Modifications and any other deliverables developed specifically for Sparkling and paid for by Sparkling, excluding any Garman intellectual property existing prior to or developed independently of this Agreement that is embedded therein, in respect of which Garman grants to Sparkling a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense such embedded Garman intellectual property as part of the Modifications and such deliverables for the purposes of Sparkling's business. Sparkling retains all right, title and interest in and to Sparkling's data and materials, including all data converted, processed or stored using the Software, and Garman acquires no rights in them. Nothing in this Agreement creates joint ownership of any intellectual property.

Comment:
[Playbook] We have carved the bespoke Schedule "D" Modifications and any other deliverables we pay for out of Garman's blanket ownership claim, with a perpetual royalty-free licence back for any embedded Garman IP, and confirmed that our data remains ours. Our playbook position is that we own what we pay for and everything we put in; if assignment is not workable we can instead accept Garman ownership of the Modifications coupled with a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense them for our business.

Rationale is accurate on the facts: the licence is not revocable at will (perpetual while fees are paid, terminable only for insolvency or uncured material breach), so the deviation is correctly scoped to affiliate/contractor coverage and transferability.

The high changed-character ratio (0.726) is explained by the necessary restructuring of the grant preamble; the operative substance of the clause (object-code/AS400 scope, Documentation, additional-fee sentence) is preserved, so the edit is proportionate rather than an over-rewrite.
Comment is accurate, concise, in the required first-person plural voice with the [Playbook] prefix, cites the playbook position and offers the affiliate-on-written-notice fallback.

Minor residual: §3(c) and §20(d) still restrict transfer/assignment. This is tolerable because §3(c)'s exception ('except as and when authorized... by Garman in writing') is satisfied by the amended written grant and §20(d) addresses assignment of the Agreement rather than the licence, but a cross-reference such as 'Notwithstanding Sections 3(c) and 20(d)' would remove any ambiguity and is worth raising in negotiation.

content.text:
**Finding: Compliant (no redline required).**

The agreement grants Garman no audit, inspection or usage-verification right against Sparkling:

- **§ 3 (Restrictions on Use)** — subsections (a)–(g) impose substantive use limits only (no copying, no reverse engineering, no service bureau use); there is no compliance-audit, self-reporting or access mechanism attached to them.
- **§ 20 (General Matters)** — limited to time-of-the-essence and notice provisions.
- **§ 14 (Confidentiality)** — mentions "accounting records for which access is obtained" only to bring such records within the definition of Confidential Information; it creates no inspection right.
- **§ 11 (Fees)** — a bare payment obligation with no true-up or usage-verification right.
- Full-text searches for *audit*, *inspect*, *verify*, *records*, *premises* and *monitor* surfaced nothing operative.

Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
Searches for "audit", "inspect", "verify", "records", "premises" and "monitor" return no verification or inspection right binding Sparkling. Restrictions on Use (§ 3, including (a)-(g)) imposes only substantive use limits with no compliance-audit, reporting or system-access mechanism; General Matters (§ 20) covers only time-of-the-essence and notices; Confidentiality (§ 14) references accounting records only as protected Confidential Information, not as an audit right; Fees (§ 11) contains no usage-verification or true-up right. Because Garman has no audit or inspection right against us, and no right of access to our systems, there is nothing to constrain and the AUDIT rule's risk (frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access) does not arise. Adding audit language would create a customer obligation that does not currently exist, so no redline is proposed.

Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position. Use fallback only when the rule guidance or existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.

ID: LD
Title: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: Service credits to us are welcome; liquidated damages against us are not.
Severity: high
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer.
Position — fallback:
Early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount.
Position — walk-away:
Liquidated damages exceeding the remaining contract value or triggered by minor breaches.
Detection guidance:
Identify liquidated damages, penalties, minimum fees on termination, "shall pay … as liquidated damages". Flag only when Customer pays. Service credits or LDs payable by Vendor to Customer are compliant.

Redline guidance:
Delete the Customer-payable LD; if an early-termination fee is unavoidable, cap it at 3 months' fees.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

input.rationale: Searches for "audit", "inspect", "verify", "records", "premises" and "monitor" return no verification or inspection right binding Sparkling. Restrictions on Use (§ 3, including (a)-(g)) imposes only substantive use limits with no compliance-audit, reporting or system-access mechanism; General Matters (§ 20) covers only time-of-the-essence and notices; Confidentiality (§ 14) references accounting records only as protected Confidential Information, not as an audit right; Fees (§ 11) contains no usage-verification or true-up right. Because Garman has no audit or inspection right against us, and no right of access to our systems, there is nothing to constrain and the AUDIT rule's risk (frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access) does not arise. Adding audit language would create a customer obligation that does not currently exist, so no redline is proposed.

content.text:
**Finding: Compliant (no redline required).**

The agreement grants Garman no audit, inspection or usage-verification right against Sparkling:

- **§ 3 (Restrictions on Use)** — subsections (a)–(g) impose substantive use limits only (no copying, no reverse engineering, no service bureau use); there is no compliance-audit, self-reporting or access mechanism attached to them.
- **§ 20 (General Matters)** — limited to time-of-the-essence and notice provisions.
- **§ 14 (Confidentiality)** — mentions "accounting records for which access is obtained" only to bring such records within the definition of Confidential Information; it creates no inspection right.
- **§ 11 (Fees)** — a bare payment obligation with no true-up or usage-verification right.
- Full-text searches for *audit*, *inspect*, *verify*, *records*, *premises* and *monitor* surfaced nothing operative.

Since no audit right binds us — and in particular no right of access to our systems — the AUDIT rule's risks (frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access) do not arise. Inserting the preferred frequency/notice/cost parameters would require first creating an audit right that Garman does not currently have, which would be worse for us than silence. Accordingly, no edit is proposed.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

input.rationale: The Agreement imposes no liquidated damages, penalties or minimum/early-termination fees on Sparkling (the Customer). Section 11 obliges Sparkling only to pay fees "as set out in the Fee Schedule" with no late-payment interest or penalty mechanic, and Section 17(b) permits Sparkling to terminate for convenience on 90 days' notice with no termination fee or payment of remaining contract value. Searches for "liquidated damages", "penalty", "interest", "damages" and fee/charge language returned no Customer-payable stipulated sums; the only "penalties" reference (p0090) is within Garman's indemnity of Sparkling, and the non-solicitation clause (Section 19) carries no fee for breach. Amounts flowing on termination run in our favour (Garman returns fees paid under Sections 8(b) and 17(c)). This satisfies the preferred position, so no redline is required.

content.text:
**Finding: Compliant (no redline required).**

The agreement grants Garman no audit, inspection or usage-verification right against Sparkling:

- **§ 3 (Restrictions on Use)** — subsections (a)–(g) impose substantive use limits only (no copying, no reverse engineering, no service bureau use); there is no compliance-audit, self-reporting or access mechanism attached to them.
- **§ 20 (General Matters)** — limited to time-of-the-essence and notice provisions.
- **§ 14 (Confidentiality)** — mentions "accounting records for which access is obtained" only to bring such records within the definition of Confidential Information; it creates no inspection right.
- **§ 11 (Fees)** — a bare payment obligation with no true-up or usage-verification right.
- Full-text searches for *audit*, *inspect*, *verify*, *records*, *premises* and *monitor* surfaced nothing operative.

Since no audit right binds us — and in particular no right of access to our systems — the AUDIT rule's risks (frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access) do not arise. Inserting the preferred frequency/notice/cost parameters would require first creating an audit right that Garman does not currently have, which would be worse for us than silence. Accordingly, no edit is proposed.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

paragraphs.text: 11. FEES
Sparkling shall pay the fees as set out in the Fee Schedule in accordance with the terms of this Agreement and the Fee Schedule.
10. MAINTENANCE AND SUPPORT

For a renewable one-year term commencing upon the Maintenance Commencement Date, subject to payment of maintenance fees in accordance with the Fee Schedule but without additional fees or charges, Garman shall provide the following Maintenance Services:
(a) SOFTWARE UPDATE SERVICE
As part of the Software Update Service, Garman shall provide to Sparkling as soon as reasonably available:
(1) corrections and bug fixes for the Software;
(2) all modifications, refinements, and enhancements ("Improvements") of the Software;
(3) new releases of the Software; and
(4) updated user manuals to support all of the above in a reasonable time frame.
(b) TELEPHONE SUPPORT SERVICE

Telephone Support Service includes Sparkling having direct telephone access to employees of Garman who have the necessary technical expertise and experience to understand and consider Sparkling's inquiries concerning the failure of Software to operate according to Specifications and to clarify Documentation that is either insufficient or unclear. Such direct telephone access shall be available in accordance with the Telephone Support Schedule. In the event that the Telephone Support Service does provide a resolution to Sparkling (acting reasonably) within 2 business days to permit the Software to meet the Specifications, then Garman shall provide Software Repair Services to address the Software failure. The existing Telephone support numbers are for Garman business hours 1-800-667-6901 or 1-306-242-6322

Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

content.text:
**Finding: Compliant (no redline required).**

The agreement grants Garman no audit, inspection or usage-verification right against Sparkling:

- **§ 3 (Restrictions on Use)** — subsections (a)–(g) impose substantive use limits only (no copying, no reverse engineering, no service bureau use); there is no compliance-audit, self-reporting or access mechanism attached to them.
- **§ 20 (General Matters)** — limited to time-of-the-essence and notice provisions.
- **§ 14 (Confidentiality)** — mentions "accounting records for which access is obtained" only to bring such records within the definition of Confidential Information; it creates no inspection right.
- **§ 11 (Fees)** — a bare payment obligation with no true-up or usage-verification right.
- Full-text searches for *audit*, *inspect*, *verify*, *records*, *premises* and *monitor* surfaced nothing operative.

Since no audit right binds us — and in particular no right of access to our systems — the AUDIT rule's risks (frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access) do not arise. Inserting the preferred frequency/notice/cost parameters would require first creating an audit right that Garman does not currently have, which would be worse for us than silence. Accordingly, no edit is proposed.

content.text:
**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

The agreement contains no liquidated damages, penalties, or minimum fees payable by Sparkling (our side):

- **Section 11 (Fees)** — Sparkling pays only the Fee Schedule amounts; there is no late-payment interest, penalty, or stipulated-sum mechanic.
- **Section 17(b) (Termination)** — we hold an unqualified right to terminate for convenience on 90 days' notice with **no early-termination fee** and no obligation to pay remaining contract value; our only exit obligations are to cease use and certify return/destruction.
- **Sections 8(b) and 17(c)** — money flows run in our favour on rejection or Garman default (return of amounts paid; conversion to a perpetual, fee-free licence).
- **Section 19 (Non-solicitation)** — mutual, with no liquidated fee for breach.
- The only reference to "penalties" (p0090) sits inside **Garman's indemnity of Sparkling**, which benefits us and is therefore not flagged.

This meets the rule's preferred position (no Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties), so the fallback 3-month cap is unnecessary. One watch item for the deal team, not a redline under this rule: the Fee Schedule itself was not in the reviewed text, so it is worth confirming it carries no late-payment interest or termination charge that would reintroduce a Customer-payable penalty.

Title: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: Service credits to us are welcome; liquidated damages against us are not.
Severity: high
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer.
Position — fallback:
Early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount.

Liquidated damages exceeding the remaining contract value or triggered by minor breaches.

The Agreement imposes no liquidated damages, penalties or minimum/early-termination fees on Sparkling (the Customer). input.quote: For the acceptance period and for a period of one year from the Maintenance Commencement Date, and thereafter for as long as the Software is covered by Maintenance Services and is used by Sparkling in accordance with this Agreement, Garman warrants that the Software shall perform in conformance with the Specifications in all material respects.
input.rationale: The software conformance warranty duration (one year from the Maintenance Commencement Date, extended while under Maintenance) meets the preferred 12-month position, and there is no implied-warranty disclaimer anywhere in the Agreement, so the express warranty is not swallowed. However, Section 12 states no remedy for breach: the only warranty-adjacent remedies are the acceptance-period rejection right in Sections 7-8 (time-limited and "in lieu of any other remedy") and Software Repair Service under Section 10(c), which is only a "best efforts" obligation conditional on a paid maintenance subscription. There is also no warranty that Garman's services (installation, data conversion, training, maintenance) will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner, no compliance-with-laws warranty, and no no-malicious-code warranty. We therefore insert a single supplemental paragraph in Section 12 adding the services standard, a repair/replace/re-perform-or-refund remedy, compliance with laws and no malicious code, leaving the existing 12-month software warranty intact.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.

Comment prefix: [Playbook].

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

paragraphs.text: 1. DEFINITIONS AND SCHEDULES
In this Agreement the following definitions shall apply:
(a) Authorized Locations means the locations listed in Schedule "C."
(b) Confidential Information has the meaning specified in Section 14.
(c) Documentation means the documentation related to use of the Software described in Schedule "B."
(d) Maintenance Commencement Date means the date that acceptance testing is successfully completed at all of the Authorized Locations.
(e) Maintenance Services means the Software Update Service, Telephone Support Service and Software Repair Service described in Section 10.
(f) Modifications means the modifications set out in Schedule "D."

(g) Person includes an individual, corporation, partnership, joint venture, trust, unincorporated organization, the Crown or any agency or instrumentality thereof or any other judicial entity recognized by law.
(h) Software means the software described in Schedule "B."
(i) Specifications means the specifications set out in Schedule "D."
(j) Work means the Software and the Documentation collectively.
The following is a summary of the Schedules, which shall form an integral part of this Agreement:
17. TERM AND TERMINATION

(a) This Agreement and the license granted under this Agreement shall remain in effect perpetually as long as fees are paid by Sparkling in accordance with the Fee Schedule and the Agreement is not otherwise terminated in accordance with this Section.

(b) Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman. input.quote: Sparkling shall pay the fees as set out in the Fee Schedule in accordance with the terms of this Agreement and the Fee Schedule.
input.rationale: Full-document sweep confirms Garman has no audit, inspection, records-examination, usage-verification or true-up right against Sparkling, and no right of access to Sparkling systems. Searches for "audit", "inspect", "verify", "records", "premises", "monitor", "report" and "certif" return nothing operative. Specifically: § 3 Restrictions on Use ((a)-(g)) imposes substantive use limits only, with no compliance-reporting or inspection mechanism; § 11 Fees is a bare payment obligation keyed to the Fee Schedule with no verification, reporting or reconciliation right; § 2 conditions off-site use on "payment of additional fees in accordance with the Fee Schedule" but gives Garman no means to inspect or audit to test that; § 14 Confidentiality mentions "accounting records for which access is obtained" only to bring such records within Confidential Information, not to create access; § 20 General Matters is time-of-the-essence and notices boilerplate. The Schedules (A-F) are listed in § 1 as forming part of the Agreement but are summary-titled only (Fee Schedule, Software/Documentation, Authorized Locations, Specifications, Implementation and Training, Telephone Support) and contain no reporting or verification machinery in the text available. The only certification obligation, § 17(b), is a one-off post-termination self-certification that Software, Documentation and Codes have been destroyed or returned - a customary wind-down confirmation by us, not a recurring vendor audit, and it involves no vendor entry, auditor or system access. Because no audit right binds us, the AUDIT parameters (frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access) do not arise, and this position is at least as favorable as the playbook preferred position. Inserting audit machinery would create a new Customer obligation and enlarge Garman's rights, so the smallest correct edit is none.

**Finding: Compliant (no redline required).**

The agreement grants Garman no audit, inspection or usage-verification right against Sparkling:

- **§ 3 (Restrictions on Use)** — subsections (a)–(g) impose substantive use limits only (no copying, no reverse engineering, no service bureau use); there is no compliance-audit, self-reporting or access mechanism attached to them.
- **§ 20 (General Matters)** — limited to time-of-the-essence and notice provisions.
- **§ 14 (Confidentiality)** — mentions "accounting records for which access is obtained" only to bring such records within the definition of Confidential Information; it creates no inspection right.
- **§ 11 (Fees)** — a bare payment obligation with no true-up or usage-verification right.
- Full-text searches for *audit*, *inspect*, *verify*, *records*, *premises* and *monitor* surfaced nothing operative.

Since no audit right binds us — and in particular no right of access to our systems — the AUDIT rule's risks (frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access) do not arise. Inserting the preferred frequency/notice/cost parameters would require first creating an audit right that Garman does not currently have, which would be worse for us than silence. Accordingly, no edit is proposed.

**Finding: deviation (medium)** — Section 12, ¶p0086.

**What's compliant:** The software conformance warranty runs for the acceptance period plus one year from the Maintenance Commencement Date (and continues while the Software is under Maintenance Services), which meets the preferred 12-month software position. Importantly, there is no "AS IS" clause and no disclaimer of implied warranties anywhere in the Agreement, so nothing swallows the express warranty.

**What's deficient:**
- **No warranty remedy.** Section 12 states the warranty but prescribes no consequence for breach. The nearest substitutes are inadequate: Sections 7–8 give a rejection/refund right only during the acceptance period and expressly "in lieu of any other remedy," and Section 10(c) Software Repair Service is a "best efforts" obligation contingent on a paid maintenance subscription.
- **No services warranty.** Installation, data conversion, training and Maintenance Services carry no professional/workmanlike standard.
- **No compliance-with-laws or no-malicious-code warranty.**

**Redline (validated, ok:true):** a single new paragraph inserted after ¶p0086 adding (a) a professional and workmanlike standard plus 90-day services conformance warranty, (b) compliance with laws, (c) no malicious code, and a repair/replace/re-perform remedy escalating to a refund if not cured within 30 days of notice. The existing 12-month software warranty is left untouched, so this is purely additive.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.


Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
The software conformance warranty duration (one year from the Maintenance Commencement Date, extended while under Maintenance) meets the preferred 12-month position, and there is no implied-warranty disclaimer anywhere in the Agreement, so the express warranty is not swallowed. However, Section 12 states no remedy for breach: the only warranty-adjacent remedies are the acceptance-period rejection right in Sections 7-8 (time-limited and "in lieu of any other remedy") and Software Repair Service under Section 10(c), which is only a "best efforts" obligation conditional on a paid maintenance subscription. There is also no warranty that Garman's services (installation, data conversion, training, maintenance) will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner, no compliance-with-laws warranty, and no no-malicious-code warranty. We therefore insert a single supplemental paragraph in Section 12 adding the services standard, a repair/replace/re-perform-or-refund remedy, compliance with laws and no malicious code, leaving the existing 12-month software warranty intact.

Original paragraphs:
p0086: For the acceptance period and for a period of one year from the Maintenance Commencement Date, and thereafter for as long as the Software is covered by Maintenance Services and is used by Sparkling in accordance with this Agreement, Garman warrants that the Software shall perform in conformance with the Specifications in all material respects.

Resolved definitions:
none

Rendered redline:
p0086: For the acceptance period and for a period of one year from the Maintenance Commencement Date, and thereafter for as long as the Software is covered by Maintenance Services and is used by Sparkling in accordance with this Agreement, Garman warrants that the Software shall perform in conformance with the Specifications in all material respects.
Garman further warrants that: (a) all Services (including installation, data conversion, training and Maintenance Services) will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards, and for a period of ninety (90) days following performance will conform in all material respects to the applicable Specifications and Documentation; (b) it will comply with all laws applicable to its performance under this Agreement; and (c) the Software as delivered will be free of any virus, worm, time bomb, disabling device or other malicious code. If any Software, Deliverable or Service fails to conform to the warranties in this Section 12, Garman shall promptly repair, replace or re-perform the non-conforming item at no charge to Sparkling and, if Garman fails to do so within thirty (30) days of written notice, Garman shall refund the fees paid for the non-conforming Software, Deliverable or Service.

Comment:
[Playbook] Section 12 gives us a twelve-month conformance warranty but no stated remedy and no warranty covering Garman's services, legal compliance or malicious code. We have added a professional and workmanlike standard for the Services, a repair/replace/refund remedy for breach, and standard compliance-with-laws and no-malicious-code warranties, consistent with our playbook position.

By virtue of this Agreement, the parties may have access to information that is confidential to one another ("Confidential Information"). (a) is or becomes publicly available through no fault of the other party;
(b) is already in the rightful possession of the other party prior to its receipt from the other party;
(c) is independently developed by the other party;
(d) is lawfully obtained by the other party from a third party;
(e) is disclosed as required by law; or
(f) is disclosed to professional advisors in confidence.

I extended the search to close the contingency the verifier flagged (a verification or true-up right hiding in fee/reporting provisions or schedules):

- **§ 11 Fees (p0084)** — bare payment obligation keyed to the Fee Schedule; no reporting, reconciliation or verification right.

That is a customary wind-down confirmation given by us, not a recurring vendor audit, and it involves no vendor entry, no third-party auditor and no system access.

Deterministic checks are heuristics (regular expressions and a changed-character ratio), not verdicts: a failed regex may simply be a phrasing variant, and a high changed-character ratio is acceptable when the rule genuinely requires rewriting the clause (for example replacing a governing-law sentence or deleting a take-or-pay obligation). Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
Full-document sweep confirms Garman has no audit, inspection, records-examination, usage-verification or true-up right against Sparkling, and no right of access to Sparkling systems. Searches for "audit", "inspect", "verify", "records", "premises", "monitor", "report" and "certif" return nothing operative. Specifically: § 3 Restrictions on Use ((a)-(g)) imposes substantive use limits only, with no compliance-reporting or inspection mechanism; § 11 Fees is a bare payment obligation keyed to the Fee Schedule with no verification, reporting or reconciliation right; § 2 conditions off-site use on "payment of additional fees in accordance with the Fee Schedule" but gives Garman no means to inspect or audit to test that; § 14 Confidentiality mentions "accounting records for which access is obtained" only to bring such records within Confidential Information, not to create access; § 20 General Matters is time-of-the-essence and notices boilerplate. The Schedules (A-F) are listed in § 1 as forming part of the Agreement but are summary-titled only (Fee Schedule, Software/Documentation, Authorized Locations, Specifications, Implementation and Training, Telephone Support) and contain no reporting or verification machinery in the text available. The only certification obligation, § 17(b), is a one-off post-termination self-certification that Software, Documentation and Codes have been destroyed or returned - a customary wind-down confirmation by us, not a recurring vendor audit, and it involves no vendor entry, auditor or system access. Because no audit right binds us, the AUDIT parameters (frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access) do not arise, and this position is at least as favorable as the playbook preferred position. Inserting audit machinery would create a new Customer obligation and enlarge Garman's rights, so the smallest correct edit is none.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

input.rationale: Section 17 addresses only Sparkling's obligation to cease use and return/destroy Garman's Software, Documentation and Codes; there is no exit-assistance obligation and no requirement for Garman to return our data (including data converted under Section 4(b)) or to delete and certify deletion. Section 14 imposes only confidentiality obligations, and Section 18 survival lists nothing on transition or data return. Searches for "transition" and "data" confirm the absence. Inserted a new Section 17(d) matching the preferred position: six months of transition assistance at then-current rates, return of our data in a machine-readable format within thirty days, and subsequent deletion with written certification.

Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position. Use fallback only when the rule guidance or existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

paragraphs.text: 14. CONFIDENTIALITY

By virtue of this Agreement, the parties may have access to information that is confidential to one another ("Confidential Information"). Confidential Information means all data and information related to the business and management of either party, including proprietary and trade secrets, technology and accounting records for which access is obtained by the other party pursuant to this Agreement, provided that such Confidential Information shall not include data or information which:
(a) is or becomes publicly available through no fault of the other party;
(b) is already in the rightful possession of the other party prior to its receipt from the other party;
(c) is independently developed by the other party;
(d) is lawfully obtained by the other party from a third party;
(e) is disclosed as required by law; or
(f) is disclosed to professional advisors in confidence.
1. DEFINITIONS AND SCHEDULES
In this Agreement the following definitions shall apply:
(a) Authorized Locations means the locations listed in Schedule "C."
(b) Confidential Information has the meaning specified in Section 14.
(c) Documentation means the documentation related to use of the Software described in Schedule "B."
(d) Maintenance Commencement Date means the date that acceptance testing is successfully completed at all of the Authorized Locations.
(e) Maintenance Services means the Software Update Service, Telephone Support Service and Software Repair Service described in Section 10.
(f) Modifications means the modifications set out in Schedule "D."

(g) Person includes an individual, corporation, partnership, joint venture, trust, unincorporated organization, the Crown or any agency or instrumentality thereof or any other judicial entity recognized by law.
(h) Software means the software described in Schedule "B."
(i) Specifications means the specifications set out in Schedule "D."
(j) Work means the Software and the Documentation collectively.
The following is a summary of the Schedules, which shall form an integral part of this Agreement:

ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.

Category: audit

No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.

Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

input.rationale: Searches for "audit", "inspect", "verify", "records", "premises" and "monitor" return no verification or inspection right binding Sparkling. Restrictions on Use (§ 3, including (a)-(g)) imposes only substantive use limits with no compliance-audit, reporting or system-access mechanism; General Matters (§ 20) covers only time-of-the-essence and notices; Confidentiality (§ 14) references accounting records only as protected Confidential Information, not as an audit right; Fees (§ 11) contains no usage-verification or true-up right. Because Garman has no audit or inspection right against us, and no right of access to our systems, there is nothing to constrain and the AUDIT rule's risk (frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access) does not arise. Adding audit language would create a customer obligation that does not currently exist, so no redline is proposed.

content.text:
**Finding: Compliant (no redline required).**

The agreement grants Garman no audit, inspection or usage-verification right against Sparkling:

- **§ 3 (Restrictions on Use)** — subsections (a)–(g) impose substantive use limits only (no copying, no reverse engineering, no service bureau use); there is no compliance-audit, self-reporting or access mechanism attached to them.
- **§ 20 (General Matters)** — limited to time-of-the-essence and notice provisions.
- **§ 14 (Confidentiality)** — mentions "accounting records for which access is obtained" only to bring such records within the definition of Confidential Information; it creates no inspection right.
- **§ 11 (Fees)** — a bare payment obligation with no true-up or usage-verification right.
- Full-text searches for *audit*, *inspect*, *verify*, *records*, *premises* and *monitor* surfaced nothing operative.

Since no audit right binds us — and in particular no right of access to our systems — the AUDIT rule's risks (frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access) do not arise. Inserting the preferred frequency/notice/cost parameters would require first creating an audit right that Garman does not currently have, which would be worse for us than silence. Accordingly, no edit is proposed.

input.rationale: Full-document sweep confirms Garman has no audit, inspection, records-examination, usage-verification or true-up right against Sparkling, and no right of access to Sparkling systems. Searches for "audit", "inspect", "verify", "records", "premises", "monitor", "report" and "certif" return nothing operative. Specifically: § 3 Restrictions on Use ((a)-(g)) imposes substantive use limits only, with no compliance-reporting or inspection mechanism; § 11 Fees is a bare payment obligation keyed to the Fee Schedule with no verification, reporting or reconciliation right; § 2 conditions off-site use on "payment of additional fees in accordance with the Fee Schedule" but gives Garman no means to inspect or audit to test that; § 14 Confidentiality mentions "accounting records for which access is obtained" only to bring such records within Confidential Information, not to create access; § 20 General Matters is time-of-the-essence and notices boilerplate. The Schedules (A-F) are listed in § 1 as forming part of the Agreement but are summary-titled only (Fee Schedule, Software/Documentation, Authorized Locations, Specifications, Implementation and Training, Telephone Support) and contain no reporting or verification machinery in the text available. The only certification obligation, § 17(b), is a one-off post-termination self-certification that Software, Documentation and Codes have been destroyed or returned - a customary wind-down confirmation by us, not a recurring vendor audit, and it involves no vendor entry, auditor or system access. Because no audit right binds us, the AUDIT parameters (frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access) do not arise, and this position is at least as favorable as the playbook preferred position. Inserting audit machinery would create a new Customer obligation and enlarge Garman's rights, so the smallest correct edit is none.

[{"id":"f-indemn-7e042c0a","ruleId":"INDEMN","ruleTitle":"Indemnification by Vendor","severity":"critical","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 13 INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY INDEMNITY","rationale":"Section 13 contains only an indemnity for breach of Garman's title/non-infringement warranty: there is no express duty to defend or settlement-control mechanic, no coverage for Garman's breach of law, data incidents or gross negligence/wilful misconduct, no extension to our affiliates, and notice is a strict ten-calendar-day condition. {"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Software License and Maintenance Agreement (Garman)

**To:** Deal team, Sparkling (Customer)
**From:** In-house counsel
**Re:** Playbook review of the Software License and Maintenance Agreement — verified findings and recommended positions

## Executive summary

We have completed our playbook review of the Garman Software License and Maintenance Agreement. The commercial architecture is workable and several areas are already at or better than our preferred position: there is no exclusivity or non-compete binding us, no minimum purchase or take-or-pay commitment, no most-favoured-nation obligation, no liquidated damages or early-termination fee, and no audit right running against us.

Three issues are critical and, in our view, must be resolved before signature. First, there is **no monetary cap on liability anywhere in the Agreement** (§ 15 excludes only indirect damages), leaving both parties — including us — with unlimited direct-damages exposure; we propose a mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees or USD 1,000,000 with a standard set of uncapped Excluded Claims. Second, **§ 13 gives Garman ownership of all IP in the Work "including any Improvements or Modifications thereto"**, which captures the bespoke Schedule "D" Modifications we commission and pay for, with no clear licence back and no confirmation that our data remains ours. Third, the **§ 13 indemnity is narrow**: it covers only breach of the title/non-infringement warranty, contains no duty to defend or settlement-control mechanic, omits breach of law, data incidents and gross negligence/wilful misconduct, does not extend to our affiliates, and conditions recovery on a strict ten-calendar-day notice.

At the high level, § 20(d) and § 3(c) impose a flat consent requirement on assignment with no affiliate, successor or reasonableness carve-out and no change-of-control provision — our stated walk-away position. The § 2 licence is likewise too narrow (affiliates only at Authorized Locations, no contractors, expressly non-transferable). Section 19 imposes a mutual outright **no-hire**, also a walk-away item, which we propose to convert to a narrow 12-month non-solicit. Remaining medium and low items include Nova Scotia governing law and venue (outside our accepted list), absent maintenance renewal mechanics and uplift cap, absent transition assistance and data return, a warranty with no stated remedy and no services/compliance/malicious-code warranties, a 90-day convenience termination notice with no refund of prepaid fees, and the absence of any vendor insurance covenant.

One finding — the AUDIT review (§ 1) — failed verification and should be re-run before we rely on it; the substantive conclusion recorded there is that no audit right binds us and no edit is required.

## Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Issue / position |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | § 13 Intellectual Property Indemnity | Indemnity limited to breach of title/non-infringement warranty; no duty to defend or settlement control, no coverage for breach of law, data incidents or gross negligence/wilful misconduct, no extension to affiliates, strict 10-day notice condition. Add defence/notice/cooperation procedure and standard additional heads; 3x annual fees super-cap available as fallback. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 13 Intellectual Property Indemnity | Garman owns all IP in the Work "including any Improvements or Modifications thereto", capturing customer-funded Schedule "D" Modifications, with no licence back (§ 2 covers only Software and Documentation) and no confirmation we retain rights in our data converted under § 4(b). Assign customer-funded Modifications to us with a licence back for embedded Garman IP, confirm our data remains ours, bar joint ownership. Fallback: Garman ownership plus perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense. |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Deviation | § 15 Limitation of Garman's Liability | No monetary cap anywhere in the Agreement; § 15 is only a mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages, the heading is one-sided, and the sole carve-out is "breaches of Sections 13 and 14". Insert mutual cap at greater of 12 months' fees or USD 1,000,000 with uncapped Excluded Claims (confidentiality, data protection/security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement), confirm fee obligations are not "damages", neutralise the heading. |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | Page 10 (§ 20(d); see also § 3(c)) | Flat consent requirement with no affiliate or M&A carve-out and no reasonableness standard (walk-away); § 3(c) additionally bars our assignment absent Garman's written authorisation; no change-of-control provision. Add affiliate/successor carve-out, reasonableness standard, competitor bar on Garman assignment, and confirm change of control is not an assignment and gives no termination or re-pricing right. |
| 5 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 2 Grant of License | Licence is perpetual while fees are paid, but covers affiliates only at Authorized Locations, omits contractors, and is expressly non-transferable with assignment barred (§ 3(c), § 20(d)), leaving no successor path.
